The existing front setback of the dwellings along a street

Source: R/front_setback.R
find_existing_front_setbacks.Rd

Some plans set a front yard by what is already there rather than by a number: the Auckland Unitary Plan's Special Character Areas set it as "the average of existing setbacks of dwellings on adjacent sites, being the three sites on either side of the subject site or six sites on one side" (D18.6.1.3.1). A yard declared yard(value_from = "existing_front_setback") takes its depth from this measurement, per road boundary.

Usage

find_existing_front_setbacks(
  sites,
  roads,
  buildings,
  streets,
  street_field = "name",
  neighbours = NULL,
  site_ids = NULL,
  rulebook = NULL,
  morphology = list()
)

Arguments

sites

Sites, sf polygons with a site_id column.

roads

Road parcels.

buildings

Building outlines (polygons).

streets

Street centre lines with a name column (street_field).

street_field

Column of streets holding the street name.

neighbours

Optional further parcels that may be neighbours (outside the sites studied, so a site at the edge sees across it).

site_ids

Sites to measure. Default all.

rulebook, morphology

Morphology settings, as for morphology.

Value

A data frame, one row per road boundary segment measured: segment_id, site_id, street, setback (NA where nothing was measured), n (dwellings averaged) and neighbours (their ids and setbacks, as "id:metres" joined by ";").

Details

For each road boundary of a site:

  1. The street is the named street line nearest the boundary's middle, merged along its length (every line sharing its name), and its corridor is the road parcels that line runs through.

  2. The adjacent sites are the parcels with at least rear_site_max_frontage of boundary on that corridor, on the same side of the street, ordered by where each meets it: front_setback_neighbours on each side, or twice that on one side where the other has fewer (a street end or a corner). A rear site or a sliver is not beside the subject along the street and is not counted.

  3. A dwelling's setback is the distance to the corridor of the front-most building on the parcel with at least front_setback_min_dwelling_area of it inside the parcel, so a garage or shed is not taken for a dwelling. A neighbour with none adds nothing and is not replaced, because the plan names which sites.

  4. The yard is the mean of the setbacks found; NA where none is.

A corner site gets a yard on each street from that street's neighbours. Building outlines traced from imagery include verandas and porches where the trace does, which a plan's "setback of dwellings" may not settle. This follows capacityengine (items 314, 317 and 325).
